goal: Produce static position-independent executables (-static-pie) for Linux bitcoind and CLI tools
Allow bitcoind release binaries to run across arbitrary Linux distros, musl systems, and scratch containers
agreement: Strong support across maintainers and contributors for static release binaries (theuni, willcl-ark, hebasto, dergoegge)
NSS drawback of disabling dynamic resolver plugins is acknowledged and documented in release notes

categories.name: build
why: P2 because it majorly expands release binary portability across Linux distributions and environments
Eliminates host glibc dependency mismatches and enables execution on Alpine musl and scratch containers
Resolves long-standing release distribution limitations without switching libc

result.summary: Updates the Guix build configuration to compile x86_64 and aarch64 Linux bitcoind and utility binaries as statically linked position-independent executables (-static-pie) using glibc 2.44 and GCC 14.3.0. The GUI binary (bitcoin-qt) continues to be dynamically linked using the existing toolchain. Includes Guix patches to remove store paths and prevent runtime dlopen in NSS, while adjusting symbol and security linters for static ELF binaries.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core's Linux release binaries depend dynamically on host glibc and related libraries, preventing them from running on systems with older glibc versions, non-glibc distributions like Alpine Linux, NixOS without helper loaders, or minimal container environments.

resolved_concerns: Static glibc builds cannot dynamically load external NSS modules (such as mDNS, SSSD, or LDAP); resolved by verifying that standard /etc/hosts and DNS resolution succeed via builtin routines, and documenting the limitation in release notes
ELF security check for FORTIFY_SOURCE fails on static binaries due to lack of dynamic symbol imports; resolved by adapting the symbol checker to recognize static ELFs
Minimum kernel version questions; addressed by pinning --enable-kernel in companion PR #35993

agreement.reason: Contributors and maintainers strongly favor static PIE release binaries for portability. Several reviewers verified reproducible builds and tested binaries on Fedora, Alpine, NixOS, Ubuntu, and container hosts.

result.card: This PR configures Guix to build Linux x86_64 and aarch64 bitcoind and utility binaries as static position-independent executables (-static-pie) using glibc 2.44, while keeping bitcoin-qt dynamically linked. This resolves portability problems for operators on non-glibc distributions like Alpine, older Linux systems, NixOS, and container runtimes. The change has strong project interest, multiple approach ACKs, and corroborated reproducible builds across reviewers, with known external NSS module limitations documented in release notes. It is based on and depends on open toolchain PRs #36272 and #36193.
